title: School finances 1: Money in a fee-paying public school
description: The school fund, the budget and fees meeting, fee exemptions, lawful collection of arrears, and the records, audit and reports the law requires, including the BELA Act changes.

lessons.title: The school fund and the SGB's money duties
lessons.summary: What the SGB must do with the school's money, and the limits the law places on it.
lessons.body:
## 🎯 Why it matters

Parents pay school fees in good faith. The South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA) makes the governing body of a public school responsible for that money. This module covers public schools only. Independent schools are run by a board of governors under their own constitution and contracts with parents, so their fee rules come from those documents, not from these sections of SASA.

## 💡 The duty to supplement state funding

The State must fund public schools on an equitable basis (SASA s34). The governing body must then "take all reasonable measures within its means" to supplement those resources to improve the quality of education for all learners (SASA s36(1)). Charging fees is one way to do this, but it is a decision for the parents, as you will see in Lesson 2.

## 🏦 One school fund, one bank account

- The governing body must establish a school fund and administer it according to directives issued by the Head of Department (HOD) (SASA s37(1), as amended by BELA s27).
- All money the school receives, including school fees and voluntary contributions, must be paid into the school fund (SASA s37(2)).
- The school must open and keep one bank account. Surplus money may be invested in another account only with the approval of the Member of the Executive Council (MEC) (SASA s37(3)).
- Donations and bequests must be used according to their conditions (SASA s37(4)).
- The fund may be used only for educational purposes at or in connection with the school, for the functions of the governing body, or for other educational purposes agreed with the HOD (SASA s37(6)).
- School fund money may not be paid into a trust or used to set up a trust (SASA s37(7)).

## ⚖️ Loans, leases and overdrafts

Since the BELA Act came into force on 24 December 2024, a governing body may not enter into any loan, lease or overdraft agreement, for any purpose, without the written approval of the HOD (SASA s36(2), as amended by BELA s26). Before BELA the rule was narrower: it covered loans and overdrafts "to supplement the school fund" and the approval came from the MEC.

> ⚠️ Watch out: "for any purpose" now catches everyday deals such as a photocopier lease. Get the HOD's written approval before anyone signs. Note that s36(3), which says a lender is not bound without approval, still refers to the MEC, so check the current approval process with your district office.

Leasing out school land or buildings for more than 12 months needs MEC approval; a lease of 12 months or less does not (SASA s36(4)(a)(i), as amended by BELA s26).

## 👥 Who does what

- The principal must assist the governing body with managing the school's funds, give advice on the financial effect of decisions, take reasonable steps to prevent financial maladministration, serve on the finance committee and report mismanagement to the governing body and the HOD (SASA s16A(2)(h) to (k)).
- The treasurer is a required office bearer (SASA s29(1)). Where reasonably practicable, the chair of the finance committee must be a parent member who is not employed at the school (SASA s29(2)(b), as substituted by BELA s23).
- A member must declare any personal or financial interest and leave the meeting before the governing body discusses procurement of goods and services in which that interest exists (SASA s26, as substituted by BELA s20).
- Governing body members may be reimbursed for necessary expenses but may not be paid for their work (SASA s27).
- The governing body may not pay a state-employed educator any extra remuneration, other financial benefit or benefit in kind without the employer's approval (SASA s38A, as amended by BELA s29). This includes fee exemptions for staff children that are not given under the exemption rules in s39 to s41.

## ✅ Key points

- All school money, including fees and voluntary contributions, goes into one school fund and one bank account (SASA s37(2) and (3)).
- The fund may only be used for educational purposes and governing body functions (SASA s37(6)).
- Any loan, lease or overdraft needs the HOD's prior written approval (SASA s36(2), as amended by BELA s26).
- Members must declare interests and recuse themselves on procurement decisions (SASA s26).
- Independent schools follow their own constitution, not these SASA sections.

lessons.title: The budget and the fees meeting
lessons.summary: How the annual budget and school fees are approved by parents, including the BELA notice, quorum and deviation rules.
lessons.body:
## 🗓️ The financial year

A public school's financial year runs from 1 January to 31 December (SASA s44). The budget is prepared in the year before it applies.

## 📝 Preparing the budget

The governing body must prepare a budget each year that shows the school's estimated income and expenditure for the next financial year, following the prescriptions the MEC publishes in the Provincial Gazette (SASA s38(1)). The State must tell schools each year enough about their state funding to let them prepare this budget (SASA s34(2)).

## 📣 The parents' meeting

Before the governing body approves the budget, it must present it to a general meeting of parents called on at least 30 days' notice, for approval by a majority of parents present and voting (SASA s38(2)).

The BELA Act tightened the notice rules (SASA s38(3), as substituted by BELA s28):

1. The budget and a document explaining it must be sent to parents through the school's usual communication channels.
2. Parents must be told that the budget and the explanation will be available for inspection at the school at least 14 days before the meeting.

### 🧮 Quorum

BELA added a quorum of 10 per cent of parents for this meeting (SASA s38(6)). If the quorum is not reached, the chairperson sets a second meeting on 14 days' notice, the principal must send the notice home with every learner at least seven days before, and no quorum is needed at the second meeting (SASA s38(7)).

> 💡 Tip: Plan the calendar backwards. If you need a second meeting, you need extra weeks. Many schools hold the budget meeting in October or November so there is time for a second attempt before January.

## 🔄 Changing the budget during the year

BELA added a new rule. If the governing body needs to deviate from the approved budget by 10 per cent or more, or to reallocate money to a purpose different from what parents approved, it must take that change to a general meeting of parents called for that purpose on at least 14 days' notice, for approval by a majority present and voting (SASA s38(4)). A document explaining the reasons must go to parents, and be available for inspection at the school at least 14 days before the meeting (SASA s38(5)). The 10 per cent quorum applies here too (SASA s38(6)).

Example: parents approved R200,000 for textbooks. Halfway through the year the SGB wants to move R60,000 of it to a new security fence. That is a reallocation to a different purpose, so it goes back to the parents.

## 💵 Setting school fees

- Fees may be charged only if a majority of parents attending the budget meeting adopt a resolution to do so (SASA s39(1)).
- The resolution must set the amount of fees, set equitable criteria and procedures for total, partial or conditional exemption, and come with a budget that allows for expected non-payment and for exemptions (SASA s39(2)).
- The governing body must implement the resolution (SASA s39(3)).
- No registration, administration or other fee may be charged except school fees (SASA s39(5)).
- A school may not charge different fees within the same grade based on the curriculum or extramural curriculum (SASA s39(6)).
- Any staff payment or benefit approved under s38A must be shown in the budget, with a money value if practicable (SASA s38A(8), as amended by BELA s29).

> ⚠️ Watch out: "School fees" includes any monetary contribution paid in relation to a learner's attendance or participation in any school programme (SASA s1). A compulsory "building levy" or "tour levy" is a school fee, and must go through the same parents' meeting and exemption process.

## ✅ Key points

- The budget goes to a parents' meeting on at least 30 days' notice, with the budget and an explanation sent out and open for inspection 14 days before (SASA s38(2) and (3)).
- BELA added a 10 per cent quorum, with a second meeting needing no quorum (SASA s38(6) and (7)).
- Deviations of 10 per cent or more, or reallocations to a new purpose, need a further parents' meeting (SASA s38(4)).
- Fees need a majority resolution of parents at the budget meeting that also sets exemption criteria (SASA s39(1) and (2)).
- No separate registration or admin fees are allowed (SASA s39(5)).

lessons.title: Exemptions and parents who have not paid
lessons.summary: Who must be exempted, how the formula works, and what a school may and may not do about unpaid fees.
lessons.body:
## 📜 The rules that apply

A parent must pay the fees set under s39 unless, or to the extent that, he or she has been exempted (SASA s40(1)). The detail is in the Regulations relating to the Exemption of Parents from Payment of School Fees in Public Schools, published as Government Notice R1052 in Government Gazette 29311 of 18 October 2006, made under SASA s39(4).

> 💡 Tip: These regulations predate BELA. Ask your district office whether any newer version has been finalised before your next fee year.

## 📋 What the school must do at admission

- The principal must tell parents the annual fee amount and how to apply for exemption, and that they are liable unless exempted. The parent and principal sign a form (Annexure A) confirming this (Exemption Regulations reg 3(1)).
- The regulations must be displayed at the school, and application information is confidential (reg 3(2) and (4)).

## 🧾 Applying for exemption

A parent applies annually in writing to the chairperson of the governing body on the Annexure B form (reg 4(1)). The governing body must decide within 30 days and notify the parent in writing, with reasons, within seven days of deciding (reg 6(1) and (9)).

### 🛡️ Automatic exemption

Total exemption is automatic for a person caring for a child in a foster home, youth care centre, place of safety or orphanage, a kinship caregiver of an orphan or abandoned child, a person who receives a social grant on behalf of a child, and a child who heads a household (reg 1, "automatic exemption"). Proof is an affidavit, a social worker's or other competent authority's confirmation, or a court order (reg 4(3)).

### 🧮 The formula

The governing body works out E = 100 x (F + A) / C, where F is the annual fee for one child, A is other compulsory monetary contributions, and C is the parents' combined annual gross income (reg 6(2)). If E is 10% or more, the parent gets total exemption. Below 2%, there is no exemption. In between, partial exemption follows a table that also counts other children at fee-paying public schools (reg 6(3) to (6)). Conditional exemption is possible for parents with circumstances beyond their control (reg 6(7)).

BELA added that a parent may give an affidavit if the other parent is untraceable or will not give income details, and a court order or other documents may support it (SASA s41(2A) and (2B), inserted by BELA s30).

## ⚖️ Appeals

A parent may appeal to the HOD (SASA s40(2)), in writing within 30 days of the decision (reg 8(1)). While the appeal runs, the governing body must take no legal action against that parent (reg 8(3)(a)(ii)).

## 🚫 What a school may NOT do

- Refuse admission because a parent cannot pay or has not paid (SASA s5(3)(a)).
- Deprive a learner of participation in any part of the school programme, or victimise the learner, including suspension from classes, verbal or non-verbal abuse, denial of access to cultural, sporting or social activities or the nutrition programme, or denial of a school report or transfer certificate (SASA s41(7)).
- Attach the home the parent lives in (SASA s41(6)).

> ⚠️ Watch out: Withholding a report or excluding a child from the Grade 7 farewell over fees is prohibited.

## ✅ Collecting arrears lawfully

The school may sue a liable parent (SASA s41(1)) but only after checking the parent does not qualify for exemption, making any partial-exemption deductions, and confirming the parent signed the prescribed form (SASA s41(4)). Alternatively, the school can act if it proves written notice, by hand or registered post, that the parent failed to apply for exemption, and three months have passed without payment (SASA s41(5)). Before acting, the governing body must also consider reasonable forms of payment other than cash (reg 6(14)).

## ✅ Key points

- Parents are liable unless exempted, and may appeal to the HOD within 30 days (SASA s40; reg 8).
- Foster parents, grant recipients and child-headed households qualify for automatic total exemption (reg 1 and reg 4(3)).
- No learner may be refused admission, victimised, or denied a report over unpaid fees (SASA s5(3)(a) and s41(7)).
- Legal action only after the s41(4) or s41(5) steps, and never against the family home (SASA s41(6)).

lessons.title: Records, audit and reporting to the HOD
lessons.summary: The financial records, annual statements, audit and quarterly reports every public school must produce.
lessons.body:
## 📚 Keeping records

The governing body must keep records of all investments, donations and funds received and spent, and of the school's assets, liabilities and financial transactions (SASA s42(a), as substituted by BELA s31). In practice this means a cash book, bank reconciliations, receipts, invoices, quotations, an asset register and minutes approving spending.

## 🗂️ Annual financial statements

As soon as practicable, and no later than three months after the end of the financial year, the governing body must draw up annual financial statements following the MEC's guidelines (SASA s42(b)). With a 1 January to 31 December year (SASA s44), that means by 31 March.

BELA added two new duties (SASA s42(c) and (d)):

1. Present the financial records and statements to a general meeting of parents.
2. Tell parents that the records and statements will be available for inspection at the school at least 14 days before that meeting.

> 💡 Tip: Many schools combine the report-back on last year's statements with another parents' meeting. If you do, make sure the notice says so and that the 14-day inspection window is met.

## 🔍 Audit or examination

- The governing body must appoint a registered auditor under the Auditing Profession Act 26 of 2005 to audit the records and statements (SASA s43(1)).
- If an audit is not reasonably practicable, it must appoint a person to examine and report on them who is qualified to act as an accounting officer under s60 of the Close Corporations Act, or approved by the MEC (SASA s43(2)).
- No person with a financial interest in the school's affairs may be appointed (SASA s43(3)). An auditor who is the treasurer's business partner, or whose firm also supplies the school, is not a safe choice.

## 📤 Reporting to the HOD

BELA substituted s43(5). A governing body must now submit to the HOD:

1. Within 30 days after the end of each quarter, a quarterly report on all income and expenditure, in the format the HOD directs (SASA s43(5)(a)).
2. Within six months after the end of the financial year, a copy of the annual financial statements, audited or examined (SASA s43(5)(b)). For a calendar year that is by 30 June.

> ⚠️ Watch out: The quarterly report is new under BELA (in force from 24 December 2024). Ask your district office which template and channel your province uses. The deadlines come from the Act itself.

## 🕵️ Investigations

If the HOD believes it is necessary, on just cause shown, he or she may authorise officials to investigate the school's finances and, where necessary after consulting the governing body, access relevant documents, ask the Auditor-General to audit the school, or appoint forensic auditors or investigators (SASA s43(4), as substituted by BELA s32). Before BELA this power sat with the MEC.

## 👀 Open books

At the request of an interested person, the governing body must make the s42 records and the audited or examined statements available for inspection (SASA s43(6)). A parent who asks to see the statements is entitled to do so.

## 🧭 A simple annual calendar

- January to March: close the books, draw up statements by 31 March (s42(b)).
- Within 30 days after each quarter (for calendar quarters, about 30 April, 30 July, 30 October and 30 January): quarterly reports (s43(5)(a)). Confirm which quarters your HOD's directive uses.
- By 30 June: audited or examined statements to the HOD (s43(5)(b)).
- Present records and statements to parents with 14 days' inspection notice (s42(c) and (d)).
- Later in the year: budget meeting for next year (s38).

## ✅ Key points

- Keep full records of money in, money out, assets and liabilities (SASA s42(a)).
- Annual statements within three months of year end, then presented to parents with 14 days' inspection notice (SASA s42(b) to (d)).
- Use a registered auditor, or a qualified examiner if an audit is not reasonably practicable, with no financial interest in the school (SASA s43(1) to (3)).
- Quarterly reports within 30 days of each quarter, audited statements within six months of year end (SASA s43(5)).
- Interested persons may inspect the records and statements (SASA s43(6)).

questions.text: Since the BELA Act, what does a governing body need before it signs a lease for a new photocopier?

options.text: Approval from a majority of parents at a general meeting
Nothing, because a photocopier lease is an operational cost
The written approval of the Head of Department
The approval of the school's auditor

questions.explanation: SASA s36(2), as substituted by BELA s26, says a governing body may not enter into any loan, lease or overdraft agreement for any purpose without the written approval of the HOD.

questions.text: How much notice must parents get of the general meeting at which the annual budget is presented?

options.text: At least 30 days
At least 7 days
At least 14 days
At least 60 days

questions.explanation: SASA s38(2) requires a general meeting of parents convened on at least 30 days' notice. The 14 days in s38(3) is the inspection period for the budget documents.

questions.text: The budget meeting fails to reach a quorum. What happens next?

options.text: The governing body may approve the budget on its own
The HOD sets the budget for the school
The meeting is postponed until 10 per cent of parents attend
A second meeting is called on 14 days' notice, and no quorum is needed at it

questions.explanation: SASA s38(6) and (7), added by BELA s28, set a 10 per cent quorum and provide that a second meeting on 14 days' notice needs no quorum.

questions.text: Mid-year the SGB wants to move money approved for textbooks to build a fence. What must it do?

options.text: Record the change in the minutes of the next SGB meeting
Present the reallocation to a general meeting of parents on at least 14 days' notice
Ask the principal to approve it
Nothing, as long as the total budget does not change

questions.explanation: SASA s38(4), added by BELA s28, requires a deviation of 10 per cent or more, or a reallocation to a different purpose, to go to a general meeting of parents on at least 14 days' notice.

questions.text: Which of these may a public school lawfully charge?

options.text: School fees adopted by a majority of parents at the budget meeting
A separate registration fee for new learners
Higher fees for learners who take a particular subject in the same grade
An administration fee for processing applications

questions.explanation: Fees need a parents' resolution under SASA s39(1). Registration, administration or other fees are banned by s39(5), and different fees within a grade based on curriculum are banned by s39(6).

questions.text: A parent receives a child support grant on behalf of her child. What exemption applies?

options.text: Partial exemption calculated with the formula
Conditional exemption only
Automatic total exemption, with proof such as an affidavit
No exemption, because grants count as income

questions.explanation: The Exemption Regulations (GN R1052 of 2006), reg 1, define automatic exemption to include a person who receives a social grant on behalf of a child. Reg 4(3) sets out the proof.

questions.text: A parent owes three months' fees. Which action is allowed?

options.text: Withholding the learner's year-end report
Stopping the learner from playing in the school's sports team
Attaching the family home after a court judgment
Suing the parent after confirming he does not qualify for exemption and the other s41(4) steps are met

questions.explanation: SASA s41(1) and (4) allow legal action only after exemption has been checked. Section 41(7) bans denying reports and sporting activities, and s41(6) bans attaching the parent's dwelling.

questions.text: Within what time must a parent appeal to the HOD against a refusal of exemption?

options.text: Within 7 days
Within 30 days after receiving the decision
Within 3 months
At any time before the end of the school year

questions.explanation: SASA s40(2) gives the right of appeal to the HOD, and reg 8(1) of the Exemption Regulations requires it in writing within 30 days after receipt of the decision.

questions.text: By when must a school with a calendar financial year send its audited annual financial statements to the HOD?

options.text: By 31 March
By 30 June
By 30 September
By 31 December

questions.explanation: SASA s43(5)(b), as substituted by BELA s32, requires the audited or examined statements within six months after the end of the financial year. With the year ending 31 December (s44), that is 30 June.

questions.text: What new reporting duty did BELA add for every public school?

options.text: A monthly cash flow report to the MEC
A report to the Auditor-General each year
A quarterly income and expenditure report to the HOD within 30 days after each quarter
A weekly bank statement to the district office

questions.explanation: SASA s43(5)(a), as substituted by BELA s32, requires a quarterly report on all income and expenditure within 30 days after the end of each quarter, following the HOD's directives.
